fatal_errors: The proposed h-BN intervention is not supported by any cited prior evidence.
The claim that h-BN will remain oxidation-resistant and lubricious in air at 800 °C is insufficiently justified; oxidation or reaction with the alloy could prevent the proposed continuous film.
The experiment omits the specified load, counterface, speed, distance, and the 200 and 600 °C conditions, so it cannot establish performance throughout the target regime.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective and proposes a clear, controlled comparison, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention of varying Mo in a Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 composite. It also misses the target strengthening and tribofilm mechanisms involving Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma phase, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature silver-molybdate glazes. Its pristine-alloy baseline differs materially from the Mo0.2 composite baseline. The falsification design is directionally useful, but testing only three temperatures under unspecified contact conditions cannot support an all-temperature claim, and SEM/EDS alone would not reliably identify h-BN or its reaction products; Raman and/or XPS would be needed. With no supporting citations and a questionable 800 °C oxidation premise, this remains a testable but presently unsupported alternative.
